title: A schedule enum with optional parameters

blocks.text: A constant can take several constructor parameters, and some of them may be absent. The page's advice is to expose a nullable parameter as an `Optional` rather than scatter `null` checks. `WorkSchedule` gives each day a `DayOfWeek`, a start and an end time as `"HH:mm"` text (both `null` on Sunday), and whether the day is required.
The constants, fields and constructor are given. Write:

items: `Optional<LocalTime> start()`: the start time, or empty when there is none.
`Duration hours()`: the time from start to end, or `Duration.ZERO` when the day has no times.
`boolean isWorkDay()`: whether the day has working times at all.
`static WorkSchedule forDate(LocalDate date)`: the constant for the date's day of the week.
`static Duration requiredHoursPerWeek()`: the total `hours()` of the **required** days only.

cases.says: Each day's constant gives its start time and length of work, and forDate() finds the constant for a date.
SUNDAY, built with no times, has an empty start(), zero hours() and is not a work day, instead of throwing.
requiredHoursPerWeek() counts only required days, so Saturday's hours are left out: 39 hours.

concepts: A nullable constructor parameter is exposed as an Optional instead of a null.
